nodes.name: Carbon paste preparation
nodes.procedure: A carbon based paste has been prepared by mixing graphene nanosheets provided by Hummers method, commercially available MWCNTs, polyvinylidene fluoride (PDVF) as a bounder, and N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) as solvent.
nodes.source_text: a carbon based paste has been prepared by mixing graphene nanosheets... More details on preparation the carbon paste is available in the SI.

nodes.name: Cobalt electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A metallic cobalt layer was deposited electrochemically in galvanostat mode using a conventional three electrode system (SAMA, 500). For this purpose, Ag/AgCl, Pt, and four different substrates (Ti and Cu sheets, commercially available steel mesh (pore size of about 30μm), and Ni foam (pore size of about 200μm) with similar geometrical surface area) were applied as reference, counter, and working electrode, respectively. A mixture of aqueous solution of CoCl₂ (0.5 M) and H₃BO₃ (0.5 M) was used as electrolyte. All depositions were performed at 5mA/cm² constant current density for 800 s resulting in an average thickness of about 4μm.

nodes.name: Cobalt activation to oxide/hydroxide
nodes.procedure: Cobalt layers immersed in 1 M KOH solutions for about 2h for activation by changing their surface from metallic to a mixture of oxide and hydroxide state. Afterward, cyclic voltammetry techniques in the same electrolyte was applied for five cycles in the range of -0.2 to 0.6 V using the treated cobalt layers coated on various substrates as the working electrode to form oxide phase, mainly Co₃O₄ and Co(OH)₂ on the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals cobalt oxide/hydroxide nanoflakes with average thickness of 100 nm and diameter of 400 nm on Cu substrate after KOH activation, with morphologies varying by substrate including flakes on Ti, grains on steel mesh, and plates on Ni foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM analysis has been used to explore how this pretreatment step influenced the sample's structure and surface morphology as is clear in Figure 1... average thickness and diameter of 100 and 400 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS O(1s) shows peaks at 530.0, 531.8, 533.7 eV for oxide, hydroxide, and adsorbed species; Co(2p) shows metallic Co at 778.2 eV disappearing after activation, with satellite peaks increasing from 25.1% to 38.7% indicating CoII/CoIII oxide/hydroxide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Figure 4a and b, it can be seen that O(1s) deconvoluted to three different peaks at 530.0, 531.8, and 533.7 eV which were attributed to oxygen in the cobalt oxide lattice, -OH groups, and water... satellite peaks under the Co(2p) peak increased from 25.1 to 38.7%

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows Co3O4 cubic, CoOOH, and β-Co(OH)2 brucite-like hexagonal phases after subtracting substrate peaks, unchanged by carbon paste.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Subtracting the peaks related to the substrate and carbonaceous support layer, all observed peaks were attributed to cobalt in the oxide, hydroxide forms: Co3O4 in cubic form, CoOOH, and Co(OH)2... The hexagonal cell of brucite-like β-Co(OH)2 has been seen in the XRD pattern in Figure 5.
